name: CONNIE
summary: CONNIE was designed for reactor CEνNS with a silicon target and has also published a dark-matter–electron scattering search using diurnal modulation. It is a multipurpose experiment with explicit dark-matter data.
detection_principle: Skipper CCDs resolve few-electron events. The diurnal-modulation analysis uses the changing path through Earth as the planet rotates to test temporal variations in strongly interacting dark-matter models.

sites.name: CONNIE laboratory beside the Angra-2 reactor
sites.location: Surface laboratory at the Angra-2 nuclear power plant, Angra dos Reis, Rio de Janeiro state

status.label: Operation / data analysis
status.evidence: A 2025 event hosted by an official Brazilian institution confirms continued project activity. A paper updated in 2026 analyzes 2021–2022 data; its publication date is not treated as a data-taking date.

collaboration.name: CONNIE Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Only verified representative institutions are listed, not a complete membership roster. See the collaboration pages and author affiliations in the references.

results.summary: The diurnal-modulation analysis of few-electron events sets surface-laboratory limits on dark-matter–electron scattering.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
